text:
If you’re heading out for sunset, you’ve got a clear, comfortable evening ahead, with the sun slipping away at 7:10. Temperatures are in the mid 60s now, skies stay clear, and a light breeze settles as the night turns noticeably cooler. We’re headed for a low near 49, likely the coolest morning of the season so far, so you’ll want a layer for an early start.

Saturday looks like the pick of the weekend for sunshine, warming from that chilly start to a high around 77. The forecast spread is a little wider than usual, from the low to upper 70s, but I’d bet on a pleasant afternoon. South winds build on the lake, with waves reaching 2 to 4 feet, so keep an eye on conditions if you’re boating. Most of Saturday night stays dry, though a shower could arrive after midnight.

  2. Rounds of showers and breezy periods will follow early Sunday and Monday mornings, with isolated to scattered showers and a chance of thunderstorms in between. Warm and humid conditions on Sunday will trend much cooler and drier on Monday.
  3. A progressive pattern will support periods of rain showers with a trough favored to move through Tuesday night into Wednesday.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): The weekend starts cool and nice here on Saturday. After the cool start Saturday morning, full sunshine will help warm us up into the 70s by the afternoon. Saturday night lows dip into the upper 50s and lower 60s. There is a chance for a spot shower overnight, but most will stay dry. Sunday starts dry with partly sunny skies overhead. Into the afternoon, we’ll have a chance for a few showers and thunderstorms as a cold front again passes through the area. High temperatures reach the mid to upper 70s for most.
